To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Hungarian public administration is a “bumpy road” of reforms.
the Hungarian administrative reforms have been the worst case scenario of Europeanization in terms of the quality and efficiency of public governance.
the Hungarian public administration is a highly politicized and over-centralized institution, which is not capable of delivering public services and policies in a proper and effective way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How did the Hungarian administrative reforms develop in the last two decades?
the following question: what has been the role of the European Union in the process of the Hungarian administrative reforms?
the question of how to make the Hungarian state more efficient and effective in order to serve the interests of citizens, and not the interests of political parties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the last two decades Hungary has experienced the most radical and the least successful reform of public administration in Europe.
the Hungarian case has been the worst-case in the East-Centric European region.
Hungary is in the middle of the road of Europeanization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hungarian administrative reforms are a good example for the worst-case scenario in East-Central European administrative reforms.
we can observe a clear tendency of over-centralization and politicization in the Hungarian public administration in the first twenty-year period.
we have been witnessing a process of political over-centralization of public administration in Hungary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the case of Hungary we can speak about the “worst-case scenario” of the Europeanization of public administration in East-Central Europe.
the Hungarian developments in administrative reforms have been the worst- case scenario of Europeanization in East-Central Europe.
the Hungarian administrative reforms have been characterized by a bumpy road of ups and downs.
